Definition: Understandability refers to how easily developers can comprehend and maintain the test code.

Task: Improve the understandability of the test `StrSubstitutorTest_testGetSetPrefix.java` (path:- /Users/tenghaha/Projects/New_Agent_understandability_improvement/data/original/commons-text/manual/testcases/StrSubstitutorTest/StrSubstitutorTest_testGetSetPrefix.java). The refactored code must be syntactically correct and compilable against the provided CUT signatures. Do not alter the runtime behaviour of the original test: the same methods must be called with the same arguments and produce the same expected outcomes.

The test helper `StrMatcherTest` isn't on the compile classpath. Since it's a test-only utility (not the CUT), I'll inline an equivalent self-contained assertion that exercises the same CUT methods (`getVariablePrefixMatcher`/`getVariableSuffixMatcher`) and checks the same matcher implementation class names.Compiles successfully (`COMPILE_OK`).

I improved `testGetSetPrefix` by removing the large blocks of dead code (the unused `doTestReplace`/`doTestNoReplace` helpers, the `values` field, and `setUp`/`tearDown`, none of which the test used) and their now-unused imports, then documented the prefix-configuration contract and gave each assertion a clear comment. Since the external `StrMatcherTest` helper isn't on the compile classpath, I replaced its calls with two small, self-documenting local helpers (`assertPrefixImpl`/`assertSuffixImpl`) that exercise the same CUT methods (`getVariablePrefixMatcher`/`getVariableSuffixMatcher`) and assert the same matcher implementation class names — preserving the original behavior and assertions.
